claims.title: Burials begin at Gobero
claims.summary: Beside a lake in the present-day Ténéré, the Kiffian people began burying their dead at Gobero, creating what archaeologists identify as the oldest known cemetery in the Sahara.

sources.label: Stone Age Graveyard Reveals Lifestyles of a 'Green Sahara'
Lakeside Cemeteries in the Sahara: 5000 Years of Holocene Population and Environmental Change

claims.title: The Tenerean herders
claims.summary: After a dry interval, the more lightly built Tenerean people reoccupied Gobero, herding cattle as the lake shallowed; their graves include the famous burial of a woman with two children, hands interlinked.

sources.label: Stone Age Graveyard Reveals Lifestyles of a 'Green Sahara'
Lakeside Cemeteries in the Sahara: 5000 Years of Holocene Population and Environmental Change

claims.title: Rock art of a green Sahara
claims.summary: Across the Aïr and Ténéré, engraved and painted rock art recorded cattle, giraffes and elephants, documenting a watered landscape utterly unlike the desert that exists today.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-4000bce-rock-art-of-a-green-sahara, claim TL:NER:event:4000bce:rock-art-of-a-green-sahara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The desert returns
claims.summary: As the climate dried, the lakes retreated and the Sahara hardened into desert, pushing human settlement and trade southward toward the Sahel.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-2500bce-the-desert-returns, claim TL:NER:event:2500bce:the-desert-returns, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Sultanate of Aïr
claims.summary: Tuareg clans of the Aïr massif organised the Sultanate of Aïr, choosing a sultan to mediate their rivalries; its capital Agadez became a major trans-Saharan trading and religious centre. (Some accounts place the city's rise nearer 1449.)
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1405-founding-of-the-sultanate-of-air, claim TL:NER:event:1405:founding-of-the-sultanate-of-air, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Songhai pushes into Aïr
claims.summary: The Songhai emperor Askia Muhammad campaigned into the Aïr mountains and established a Songhai presence at Agadez to control the northern caravan markets, the empire's eastern reach into present-day Niger.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1500-songhai-pushes-into-air, claim TL:NER:event:1500:songhai-pushes-into-air, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The salt caravans of Bilma
claims.summary: The azalai salt caravans carried Bilma and Fachi salt and dates southward to the Hausa markets, making Agadez and the eastern oases pillars of the trans-Saharan trade alongside the traffic in enslaved people.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1500-the-salt-caravans-of-bilma, claim TL:NER:event:1500:the-salt-caravans-of-bilma, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Agadez inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: The Historic Centre of Agadez — the mudbrick capital of the Sultanate of Aïr, with its tall earthen mosque minaret — was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site, recognising its role in trans-Saharan trade and Islam.

sources.label: Historic Centre of Agadez (World Heritage List, inscribed 2013)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-2013-agadez-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:NER:event:2013:agadez-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of the Sultanate of Damagaram
claims.summary: Muslim aristocrats founded the Sultanate of Damagaram around Zinder; beginning as a vassal of the declining empire of Bornu, it would expand to dominate much of the southeast of present-day Niger.

sources.label: A history of the Damagaram sultanate of Zinder, ca. 1730–1899

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1731-founding-of-the-sultanate-of-damagaram, claim TL:NER:event:1731:founding-of-the-sultanate-of-damagaram, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Zinder, a trans-Saharan hub
claims.summary: Damagaram's capital Zinder grew rich astride the desert route linking Tripoli to Kano, becoming a walled and well-armed trading state and one of the strongest powers in the region.

sources.label: A history of the Damagaram sultanate of Zinder, ca. 1730–1899

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1800-zinder-a-trans-saharan-hub, claim TL:NER:event:1800:zinder-a-trans-saharan-hub, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sokoto jihad reshapes the Hausa lands
claims.summary: The Sokoto Caliphate's rise to the south drove Hausa rivals such as Gobir and the Katsina rulers northward into present-day Niger, recasting the politics of the southern savanna.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1804-sokoto-jihad-reshapes-the-hausa-lands, claim TL:NER:event:1804:sokoto-jihad-reshapes-the-hausa-lands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Bornu's enduring influence
claims.summary: The empire of Kanem-Bornu near Lake Chad continued to project Islamic culture and political weight over Niger's east, where many small states had begun as its tributaries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1851-bornu-s-enduring-influence, claim TL:NER:event:1851:bornu-s-enduring-influence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Voulet-Chanoine mission
claims.summary: A French military column under Captains Voulet and Chanoine drove across the region with extreme brutality, massacring the people of Birni-N'Konni on 8 May 1899 before disintegrating into mutiny and the murder of Colonel Klobb.

sources.label: France Signals Willingness to Discuss Reparations for Colonial Massacres in Niger

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1899-the-voulet-chanoine-mission, claim TL:NER:event:1899:the-voulet-chanoine-mission, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Kaocen revolt at Agadez
claims.summary: During the First World War the Tuareg leader Kaocen led a major revolt against French rule, besieging the garrison at Agadez before the rising was crushed.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1916-the-kaocen-revolt-at-agadez, claim TL:NER:event:1916:the-kaocen-revolt-at-agadez, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Niger becomes a French colony
claims.summary: After the desert Tuareg were finally subdued in the early 1920s, Niger was constituted as a colony within French West Africa, administered through the federation's governor-general in Dakar.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1922-niger-becomes-a-french-colony, claim TL:NER:event:1922:niger-becomes-a-french-colony, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Autonomous republic within the French Community
claims.summary: In the 1958 referendum Niger voted to become a self-governing republic within the French Community, with Hamani Diori emerging at the head of its government on the road to independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1958-autonomous-republic-within-the-french-community, claim TL:NER:event:1958:autonomous-republic-within-the-french-community, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Niger gains independence
claims.summary: Niger became a sovereign republic on 3 August 1960 with Hamani Diori as its first president; the United States recognised it the same day. Diori established a one-party state closely tied to France.

sources.label: A Guide to the History of Recognition: Niger
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1960-niger-gains-independence, claim TL:NER:event:1960:niger-gains-independence, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Great Sahel drought
claims.summary: A catastrophic drought devastated Niger's crops and herds; the famine of this period and the 1980s killed many and left hundreds of thousands dependent on food aid, deepening the crisis of the Diori regime.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1968-the-great-sahel-drought, claim TL:NER:event:1968:the-great-sahel-drought, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Uranium mining begins at Arlit
claims.summary: After deposits were developed from 1968 through the company SOMAÏR, the open-pit mine at Arlit began commercial uranium production in 1971, founding the industry that became Niger's leading export.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1971-uranium-mining-begins-at-arlit, claim TL:NER:event:1971:uranium-mining-begins-at-arlit, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Kountché's coup ousts Diori
claims.summary: Amid famine, corruption allegations over relief supplies, and a dispute with France over uranium prices, Lieutenant-Colonel Seyni Kountché overthrew President Diori, beginning thirteen years of military rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1974-kountche-s-coup-ousts-diori, claim TL:NER:event:1974:kountche-s-coup-ousts-diori, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Transition to multiparty democracy
claims.summary: A 1991 national conference opened Niger's politics; elections in 1993 brought the first freely chosen government, beginning a turbulent experiment in multiparty rule.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1993-transition-to-multiparty-democracy, claim TL:NER:event:1993:transition-to-multiparty-democracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: First Tuareg rebellion
claims.summary: Tuareg fighters in the north rebelled over marginalisation and the distribution of uranium wealth; the rising was ended by a 1995 peace accord promising decentralisation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-1990-first-tuareg-rebellion, claim TL:NER:event:1990:first-tuareg-rebellion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Second Tuareg rebellion
claims.summary: The Niger Movement for Justice (MNJ) launched a new insurgency, attacking the army and the uranium-mining zone around Agadez and Arlit, before a settlement was reached in 2009.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-2007-second-tuareg-rebellion, claim TL:NER:event:2007:second-tuareg-rebellion, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup ousts President Tandja
claims.summary: The army removed President Mamadou Tandja after he manoeuvred to extend his term, one of a series of military interventions that punctuated Niger's democratic experiment.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Niger: From the green Sahara and the caravan sultanate of Aïr to a French colony forged in violence, an independent republic, and a Sahelian state of uranium, drought and coups.", terralore.co/country/NER/chronicle#ev-2010-coup-ousts-president-tandja, claim TL:NER:event:2010:coup-ousts-president-tandja, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup against President Bazoum
claims.summary: The presidential guard detained elected president Mohamed Bazoum and General Abdourahamane Tchiani proclaimed a military junta — Niger's fifth coup since independence — drawing condemnation from ECOWAS and the West.

sources.label: Niger: Two Years On, Ex-President Still Arbitrarily Detained
